blocks.text: Welcome to The B-Side! Here we talk about movie stars! Not the movies that made them famous or kept them famous, but the ones that they made in between.

Today we talk about one of the more underappreciated actors from the Golden Age of Hollywood: Robert Ryan ! Our B-Sides include Tender Comrade , Inferno , The Crooked Road , and Executive Action . Our guest is Marya E. Gates , incredible writer, film programmer, and a devoted fan of Ethan Hawke . The three of us bond over our love of Hawke, and find parallels between him and Robert Ryan .

We discuss his rise to stardom and his steadfast place on the B-picture circuit throughout his career. There’s also his progressive politics and the great irony of Ryan playing primarily villains with hateful prejudices on screen. There’s also his long friendship with Odds Against Tomorrow co-star and political ally Harry Belafonte.

Marya, Conor, and I marvel at how Ryan got better as he got older, culminating in three incredible posthumous performances ( The Outfit , The Iceman Cometh , Executive Action ) in 1973. We collectively can’t believe Executive Action was made only a decade after the JFK Assassination and correctly predicted so much of the horribleness in which our country is currently embroiled.
